main.description: A single piece of copper cookware in someone's collection. Written to the author's own repo — the PDS is whatever their identity already uses (bsky.social for most people), so no account migration is needed to participate. Only 'title' and 'createdAt' are required; a phone photo and a name is a valid post, and every descriptive field is optional so nobody is blocked on knowing their pan's gauge.

title.description: What the owner calls it. e.g. '3.5mm Dehillerin rondeau' or 'flea market mystery saucepan'.

createdAt.description: When this record was written. Not when the pan was made — see 'era' for that.

notes.description: Free text. The story, the find, what it cooks well, what's wrong with it.

photos.description: Photos of the pan. Blobs live in the author's own repo; the app view proxies and caches them for display.

maker.description: Marked maker or retailer. e.g. 'Mauviel', 'Falk', 'E. Dehillerin', 'Duparquet', 'Waldow'. Free text rather than an enum — the long tail of unmarked and obscure French and American makers is most of the interesting material.

lining.description: Interior lining. Tin is traditional and wears out; stainless is modern and doesn't. Unlined is correct for sugar and jam work.

form.description: Vessel form. Uses the names the collecting community actually uses rather than retail marketing terms.

diameterMm.description: Rim diameter in millimetres. The primary size figure for copper — collections are usually described in mm even in the US.

heightMm.description: Wall height in millimetres, excluding handle.

thicknessMm.description: Wall gauge in millimetres. The number collectors care about most: under 1.5mm is decorative, 2.5mm is a working standard, 3mm+ is professional weight.

weightG.description: Total weight in grams. A useful cross-check on stated gauge.

handleMaterial.description: Handle metal. Often the best dating evidence on an unmarked piece — cast iron reads older and French, brass reads earlier still.

era.description: Approximate period, as loose text rather than a date. e.g. 'late 19th c.', '1950s', 'modern production'. Deliberately not a datetime — almost nobody knows the real year, and a fake-precise field invites fake-precise answers.

restoration.description: What's been done to it and by whom. Retinner, date, cost, how it turned out.

provenance.description: Where it came from. Estate sale, inherited, a specific dealer, a flea market in a specific town.

acquiredAt.description: When the current owner got it, if they want to record that.

tags.description: Owner-chosen labels. Intentionally free-form — the app view aggregates these rather than dictating them.

photo.description: One photo. Mirrors the shape of app.bsky.embed.images#image so anyone who has worked with Bluesky embeds already knows this structure.

image.description: The image blob, stored in the author's own repo. 2MB ceiling — clients should resize before upload rather than relying on this to reject.

alt.description: Alt text. Required rather than optional, deliberately: this is a small community site and there is no reason to make accessibility opt-in.

aspectRatio.description: Pixel dimensions of the source image, used to reserve layout space before the image loads. Ratio only — not a promise about the served resolution.
